edit.description: the merge stage is driven per finished attempt rather than once over a settled batch
the stage takes one finished attempt under the ship lock, the ledger write and the wave's facts unchanged in what they name
the as-it-finishes arm, beside the batch-merge cases it replaces

summary: A wave holds every merge until its slowest agent finishes, so a two-minute entry's span waits on a fifteen-minute one before it reaches trunk

per.section: Fanout and worktrees — provisioning, isolation, teardown

acceptance: each entry's span is carried onto the trunk as its own agent finishes, under the ship lock, from the tip as it then stands — never in one stage after every attempt in the wave has settled; the per-entry merge isolation, the ledger write and the footprint the verdict reports are unchanged
tests: a wave merges a finished entry while a slower sibling's agent is still running
notes: Field report, 0.19, and this repo's own 31%-of-slot-time idle measurement. The lock the rolling wave needed exists (`spec/loop.md`, *The ship lock and the worktree lock — sibling ticks take turns at git*); `runWaveMerge` (`src/waveMerge.ts:269`) is today called once at `src/waveTick.ts:298`, after a `Promise.all` over every attempt. Half one of the ruling; the freed slot's refill is THE-FREED-SLOT-PULLS-THE-NEXT-DISJOINT-ENTRY, chained behind this.
